html:
The Kija, also spelt Gija, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the east Kimberley in Western Australia, in the country around Warmun (Turkey Creek) and the Bungle Bungle Range. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours were the Jaru to the south, the Wurla and Ngarinyin to the west and the Miriwoong to the north. The Halls Creek gold rush of 1885 and the cattle stations that followed brought violence to their country, including the killing of Kija people at Mistake Creek in 1915.

The Bungle Bungle Range, with its striped beehive domes, is now Purnululu National Park, a World Heritage site since 2003. From the 1980s Kija painters at Warmun, using natural ochres, became some of the best known Aboriginal artists in Australia.
